clue.text: Inattentive sailor dismissed

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard crossword sailor
sent away, as in sent packing

explanation.surface: A daydreaming sailor gets thrown off the ship for not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: AB plus SENT gives ABSENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose mind has wandered off is described as absent, as in an absent look or absent-minded.

clue.text: Drug research facility raised a bundle

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
short for laboratory

explanation.surface: Police raid a drug laboratory and come away with a bundle.
explanation.walkthrough: E and LAB are joined, then the whole is turned upward to give BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bale is a large tightly bound package of hay, cotton or similar goods.

clue.text: Lyrical piece from rap act on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the words are taken as spoken sounds

parts.note: a rap at the door is a knock
a variety act is a turn

explanation.surface: A radio DJ plays a gentle, lyrical track lifted from a rap act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' looks like the music genre, but it means a knock; said aloud, knock-turn gives NOCTURNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy, song-like composition for piano, most famously by Chopin, evoking night.

clue.text: Henry getting on in government farm

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
getting on in years means growing old
taken as written
G is a standard abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Henry, ageing, is now in charge of agriculture in the government.
explanation.walkthrough: H, OLD, IN and G run together to give HOLDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding is a piece of land rented or owned for farming, as in a smallholding.

clue.text: Curse looms over female spirit

indicators.note: something that looms over another overhangs and hems it in, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a bane is a curse or source of ruin
the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A curse hangs ominously over a woman who is haunted by a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female spirit' wants to be the definition, but female is wordplay and spirit alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a wailing supernatural being whose cry foretells a death in the family.

clue.text: Where breakfast is served for dippy soldiers?

definitions.text: Where breakfast is served for dippy soldiers?

parts.words: Where breakfast is served for dippy soldiers?
parts.note: surface reading: a mess hall where daft troops are given their morning meal
setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, and this holds the egg

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are thin fingers of buttered toast, a British nursery breakfast dunked into a runny boiled egg; 'dippy' means made for dipping, not foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: The small cup holding a boiled egg upright is exactly where toast soldiers get dipped at breakfast.

clue.text: Reasonable European supports Spain intermittently

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last
intermittently means on and off, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of Spain
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sensible European gives occasional backing to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN with E placed below it gives SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sane describes someone of sound mind and sensible judgement, so it is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Zonked out deadbeats without a base for sleep

indicators.note: zonked out means knocked senseless, so the letters lose their order
without tells you to leave something out of the word it governs

parts.note: taken as written
the single letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Exhausted layabouts collapse with nowhere proper to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one A from DEADBEATS and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, the structure that holds the mattress up.

clue.text: Endlessly daring love: Good for you!

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: brave means bold, daring
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Applauding someone's boundless daring in love.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVE loses its last letter, then O follows to make BRAVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cheer of approval, the same congratulatory exclamation as well done.

clue.text: Agreed on a fizzy drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone settles on a soft drink with bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fizzy drink' reads as one phrase, but fizzy is the signal and drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweetened carbonated soft beverage flavoured with orange juice.

clue.text: Voted in because put up with changing sides

indicators.note: sides are right and left, so one side letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: putting up a building is erecting it

explanation.surface: Someone was voted into office because they tolerated changes of party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like tolerated, but put up is ERECTED, and its R for right becomes L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who is elected has been chosen for a post by ballot.

clue.text: Win over America with two hundred and three points

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them
compass points east, south and south

explanation.surface: Winning over America by hitting two hundred and three points in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win over' reads as persuade, but Win alone is the definition and over flips US.
explanation.definitionFit: A success is a triumph or victory, so the noun win fits it directly.

clue.text: Ability to digest cereal (not processed)

indicators.note: processed food has been broken down and reworked, so the letters are reworked too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being able to stomach unprocessed cereal, a dietary label.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'not processed' look like a food label; in fact NOT joins CEREAL as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance to a food means the body can handle eating it without ill effects.

clue.text: Bring up a kid to sponge

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to kid someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: Raising a child to scrounge off others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up a kid' suggests parenting, but kid is a verb meaning fool; A and FOOL turned upward give LOOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is the dried fibrous pod of a gourd used as a bath scrubber.

clue.text: Tart embracing Queen causes umbrage

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals hugging the Queen offends someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' plays on its slang sense for a promiscuous woman; here it is the pastry dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of irritation from wounded pride, which is what taking umbrage is.

clue.text: When to invade French who are not the real deal?

indicators.note: an invading force goes inside another's territory

parts.note: qui is French for who
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Asking when to invade the French people who are fakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' can mean when, as in 'as I left the house'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasi means seemingly or partly but not genuinely, like a quasi-official body.

clue.text: Gems for 28 pounds or more

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, so two or more of them

explanation.surface: Paying 28 pounds or more for some jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds looks like money, but it is weight; the stone is a British unit of 14 pounds still used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious jewels are called stones, and a weight of two or more fourteen-pound units is also this plural.

clue.text: 1st class British capital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, of the highest quality
second meaning: the currency of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Travelling first class to London.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like a city such as London; here it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes admirable quality, as in sterling work, and names the British pound as currency.

clue.text: Extreme characters into complicated risk

indicators.note: into means going inside something, so these letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: hard as in difficult
A and Z are the letters at each end of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Going to extremes turns a tricky situation into a dangerous one.
explanation.walkthrough: Extreme characters means the letters at the two ends of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a danger or source of peril, so it means the same as a risk.

clue.text: War cries disturbed high-flying employees

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Battle shouts upset ambitious staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flying' usually means successful, but here it is literal: these staff work in planes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrews are the pilots and cabin staff who work aloft on an aeroplane.

clue.text: Overlook setter's memorandum

parts.note: to overlook something is to miss it
the setter has, from the setter's point of view, is I've

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter's memo gets overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's stands for setter has: the setter calls himself I, so I have becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a written message or letter, much like an official memo.

clue.text: Detail of couple dating exists on-line

parts.note: a dating couple are said to be an item
is means exists
E stands for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Details of a couple who met through online dating.
explanation.walkthrough: ITEM, IS and E join to give ITEMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list item by item, which is to set out in detail, a verb.

clue.text: Reflex actions essentially spot-on

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Reflex responses are basically accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of Reflex and the start of actions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is informal for precisely right, and exact means correct in every detail.

clue.text: Judge boxing final with it

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
the final is the end

explanation.surface: A judge at a boxing final looking fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing looks like the sport; it means enclosing one word in another.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it is old slang for being fashionable and up to date, which is what trendy means.

clue.text: Look after Italian team's selection test

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece later in the answer

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club
to look is to view

explanation.surface: Checking out an Italian football club's trial for picking players.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is: Look after Italian team is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is a formal meeting to assess candidates and choose one for a job or place.

clue.text: Rambler's act upset royal deer regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law
K stands for king

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of deer

explanation.surface: A hiker's disturbance of the king's deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal deer' reads as one phrase, but royal gives K for king and the deer is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is someone who walks in the countryside for pleasure, a hiker.

clue.text: Stores of unusually rare LSD

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Stockpiles of unusually rare hallucinogenic drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Stores is a noun here, the plural of a store-cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Larders are pantries or storerooms where food is kept, so they are stores.

clue.text: Girl got up for some wine

definitions.meaning: second meaning: past tense of rise
third meaning: pink wine, spelt with an accent in French

explanation.surface: A young woman got up to fetch some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, the past tense of the verb to rise, and pink rosé wine without its accent.

clue.text: Reported US police chief as belligerent

indicators.note: reported means told by word of mouth, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a US marshal is a federal law officer or the head of a police department

explanation.surface: An American police chief is said to be aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means warlike or relating to fighting, as in martial arts, so it is belligerent.

clue.text: Goddess lives twice

indicators.note: twice tells you to write the piece two times in a row

parts.note: is means lives or exists
the same piece repeated

explanation.surface: A goddess who lives two lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the principal mother goddess of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Falls headlong from dingy bars, following smell of wine

indicators.note: following puts the first-named piece after the second in the answer

parts.note: a wine's nose is its aroma
a dive is a seedy bar

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles out of grotty bars after sniffing too much wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosedive is to plunge steeply downward, like an aircraft falling head first.

clue.text: Tiny bit edgy initially, like half the men on board?

definitions.text: like half the men on board?

parts.note: a whit is a very small amount

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of edgy

explanation.surface: A slightly nervous sailor, like half the crew aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a chessboard, where one side's pieces are this colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, sixteen of the thirty-two pieces are the pale colour, so half the men share it.
